saw_lines: People buy an outdoor blanket for one trip, then reorder when the next trip or a gift comes up.
So a first-time buyer decides in the opening line whether the blanket fits the trip and whether to act now.
Your site offers 15% off a first order, yet only 2 of 20 copy ads mention it, so put it in the first line of three new ads and on the creative.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 18 Oct 2026
points: Your site offers 15% off a first order, but only 2 of 20 copy ads mention it. A first-time buyer has no reason to act. Put the offer in the opening line of three new ads and on the creative.

None of your 20 copy ads carries a proof number, so new buyers have nothing concrete to weigh against the price. Pick one real figure, such as orders shipped, and lead the next batch with it on the creative.

Your 20 copy ads open with 12 different stories, and the biggest opens 4 of them. Spread this thin, no single story builds recognition, so each ad starts cold. Pick the two strongest stories and build the next batch from them.

All 29 ads use the same Shop now button, so every viewer gets one ask, whether they are camping or buying a gift. Match the button to each page. Shop the Puffy for Puffy ads, Shop kids for the kids collection.
